items.gloss_en: main verb plus vector — what a compound verb is

learn.title_en: Two verbs, and still only one thing happening
learn.explanation_en: Hindi very often uses two verbs where English uses one. मैंने खाना खा लिया has खा, the bare stem of खाना, followed by लिया from लेना. Only one thing is happening — eating. The second verb is not a second action; it is a shade of meaning, saying how the action landed, who it was for, whether it finished. Grammar books call the second verb a vector. There are four you need — लेना, देना, जाना, पड़ना — and this module takes them one at a time. The shape never varies: the main verb goes to its bare stem, खाना to खा, समझना to समझ, करना to कर, and the vector takes every ending.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both are correct Hindi. The vector adds that the eating is finished and settled; the plain form simply reports it.

examples.note: खा is the bare stem; लिया carries the tense and the agreement.
Also correct. No vector, no extra shading.
आ plus गया. Two verbs, one arrival.

common_error.why_en: The main verb must be a bare stem. खाया is already inflected and cannot stand in front of a vector.

practice.question: मैंने खाना ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: Bare stem खा, then the vector लिया. Only the vector inflects.

game.question_en: You simply want to report that you ate, with no extra shading.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct Hindi. The plain perfective खाया is the neutral report. खा लिया adds completion, खा दिया turns the action outward, and the last is habitual.

items.gloss_en: the vector carries tense, gender, number and ने

learn.title_en: The second verb does all the work
learn.explanation_en: Once you have written the stem it never changes again. Tense, gender, number and even the ने question are all decided by the vector. मैंने किताब पढ़ ली — पढ़ is fixed, and ली is feminine because किताब is feminine. That is Module 9 still running: with ने the verb agrees with the object, and in a compound the vector is the verb. The ने question is the part to watch, and the rule is stricter than it first looks: ने appears only when the main verb and the vector are BOTH transitive. खा लिया has transitive खाना and transitive लेना, so मैंने. खा गया has transitive खाना and intransitive जाना, so वह — no ने at all, which is the surprise waiting in level 7. And रो दिया has intransitive रोना, so no ने either, whatever देना is doing on its own.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both correct. Note that the feminine ending lands on ली in the first and on पढ़ी in the second — it is always on the last verb in the phrase.

examples.note: किताब is feminine, so the vector is ली.
पैसे is masculine plural, so दिए.
Both आना and जाना are intransitive, so there is no ने anywhere in the sentence.

common_error.why_en: Only the vector inflects. The main verb stays a bare stem no matter what the object is.

practice.prompt_en: The object is चिट्ठी. Complete the compound.
practice.question: मैंने चिट्ठी लिख ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: चिट्ठी is feminine singular, so the vector is दी.

game.question_en: You wrote the letter out for them, and it is done.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. दी turns the action outward, which is what "for them" needs. ली would keep the letter with you, and the first simply reports the writing.

items.gloss_en: without a vector — still correct Hindi

learn.title_en: A sentence with no vector is not a broken sentence
learn.explanation_en: This needs saying plainly, because it is the thing most likely to go wrong in your head over the next seventeen levels. मैंने खाना खाया is correct, natural, everyday Hindi. It is not a beginner's version of मैंने खाना खा लिया. The two mean slightly different things, and there are contexts where the plain one is better — neutral narration, a list of events, anything where you do not want to draw attention to how the action landed. What is true is that speech with no vectors at all sounds flat, because native speakers reach for them constantly. So the skill is not "always add a vector". It is knowing which shade you want, including none. Habitual statements in particular usually take no vector at all.

vectorless_equivalent.with_vector: मैं रोज़ खाना खा लेता हूँ।
vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Here the plain form is the natural one. Vectors sit badly with habitual statements, because there is no single completed action to shade.

examples.note: Complete, correct, neutral.
Finished, and the point is that it is done.

examples.hindi: कल मैं दिल्ली गया और वहाँ दो दिन रुका।
examples.read_as: kal maiṁ dillii gayaa aur vahaaṁ do din rukaa.
examples.english: Yesterday I went to Delhi and stayed two days.
examples.note: Plain narration. Adding vectors here would make it fussy.

common_error.wrong: मैं रोज़ खाना खा लेता हूँ।
common_error.why_en: Vectors shade a single completed action. For something you do every day there is nothing to shade, so the plain form is what you want.

practice.prompt_en: A plain habitual statement. Pick the natural form.
practice.question: मैं रोज़ खाना ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: Habituals normally take no vector. The others are all possible sentences but none of them is what "every day" wants.

game.question_en: You are narrating what happened, with no emphasis on how it finished.
game.explanation_en: Every option here is good Hindi. Plain खाया is the narrator's form; the first two shade the completion, and the last describes it in progress.

summary.recap_en: A compound verb is a bare stem plus a vector, and the vector carries everything — tense, gender, number, and whether the sentence takes ने. The main verb never inflects. And a sentence with no vector is correct, neutral Hindi, not a mistake.
summary.next_up_en: Next: लेना, the vector that turns the action inward.

items.pronunciation_notes: खा is one long syllable and it never changes, however the rest of the sentence moves.

learn.title_en: लेना keeps the result with the subject
learn.explanation_en: लेना as a vector says the action is complete and its result stays with the subject. मैंने खाना खा लिया is "I've eaten", with the sense that the eating is done and it was mine to do. Compare मैंने खाना खाया, which simply reports the event. Neither is wrong; they answer different questions. खा लिया is what you say when somebody asks whether you have eaten yet. लेना is transitive, so the compound takes ने and the vector agrees with the object — खाना is masculine, hence लिया.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both correct. लिया answers "have you eaten?"; the plain form answers "what did you do?"

examples.note: Completion, and the natural answer to "have you eaten?"
The question this form exists for.
रोटी is feminine, so the vector is ली.

common_error.why_en: लेना is transitive, so the compound takes ने even though nothing about खाना changed.

practice.prompt_en: You finished eating, for yourself. Pick the vector.
practice.question: मैंने खाना खा ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: लिया keeps the result with you. दिया would send it outward.

game.question_en: Someone asks whether you have eaten. You want to say yes, it's done.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct Hindi. खा लिया is the one that answers the question, because the point is that the eating is finished.

items.pronunciation_notes: समझ ends on an aspirated jh with no vowel after it: sa-majh.
items.gloss_en: to get it — understanding that has landed

learn.title_en: लेना with nothing to agree with
learn.explanation_en: समझ लिया is "got it" — understanding that has arrived and stayed. There is no object in the sentence, so the vector has nothing to agree with and falls back to the neutral masculine singular, exactly as it did with को-marked objects in Module 9. मैंने समझ लिया is what you say to show that an explanation has worked, and it is warmer and more final than मैं समझता हूँ. The plain मैंने समझा does exist, but it leans towards "I took it to mean" rather than "I understood", so this is one place where the vector is usually the better choice.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both grammatical. मैंने समझा tends towards "I took it to mean", so the vector form is the ordinary way to say you have understood.

examples.note: No object, so the neutral लिया.
Imperative of the compound; लो is the तुम form of लेना.
बात is feminine, so ली.

common_error.why_en: Only the vector inflects. समझ stays a bare stem whatever else is in the sentence.

practice.prompt_en: You have fully understood. Pick the vector.
practice.question: मैंने समझ ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: The understanding stays with you, so लेना. दिया would mean you explained it to somebody else.

game.question_en: You want to tell someone their explanation worked and you have understood.
game.explanation_en: Every option is grammatical. समझ लिया is the one that says the understanding has landed; the first is a general statement, the third sends the explaining outward, and the fourth leans towards "I took it to mean".

items.gloss_en: to get it done — the job is off your list

learn.explanation_en: कर लेना is completion with the sense that the job is off your list. मैंने काम कर लिया, I've done the work. It is one of the highest-frequency compounds in the language and worth having ready to say. काम is masculine, so the vector is लिया. And a करना verb built on a noun behaves the same way — मैंने मदद कर ली, with feminine मदद pulling the vector to ली, exactly as it did back in Module 9.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both correct. कर लिया says the job is finished and behind you; किया reports that you did it.

examples.note: काम is masculine, so लिया.
मदद is feminine, so ली — the noun inside the verb still decides.

examples.english: You go ahead and do this.
examples.note: Imperative, and gentler than plain करो.

common_error.why_en: लेना is transitive, so ने is required on the subject.

practice.prompt_en: The object is मदद. Complete the compound.
practice.question: मैंने मदद कर ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: मदद is feminine singular, so the vector is ली.

game.question_en: You want to say the job is finished and off your list.
game.explanation_en: All four are good sentences. कर लिया closes it off for you; कर दिया would suggest you did it for somebody else.

summary.recap_en: लेना completes the action and keeps its result with the subject. खा लिया, समझ लिया, कर लिया. It is transitive, so the compound takes ने, and the vector agrees with the object — never the main verb.
summary.next_up_en: Next: लेना with a feminine object, and with itself as its own vector.

levels.title_hi: पढ़ ली · ले लिए · बना लिया

items.pronunciation_notes: पढ़ uses the flapped ṛh — the tongue flicks down off the roof of the mouth.
items.gloss_en: to read through — and where the gender lands

learn.title_en: The vector takes the gender, not the main verb
learn.explanation_en: मैंने किताब पढ़ ली. किताब is feminine, and it is ली that goes feminine — पढ़ does not move at all. This is Module 9 still running: with ने the verb agrees with the object, and in a compound the vector is the verb. If you catch yourself writing पढ़ी ली, that is the Module 9 instinct firing one word too early. The rule to carry is simple: whatever the object's gender and number, it lands on the last verb in the phrase and nowhere else.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both correct, and both feminine — the ending simply sits on a different word. The vector adds that you finished it.

examples.note: किताब is feminine, so ली.
अख़बार is masculine, so लिया. Only the vector moved.
चिट्ठी is feminine, so ली again.

common_error.why_en: Only one word in the compound inflects, and it is the vector.

practice.prompt_en: The object is किताब. Complete the compound.
practice.question: मैंने किताब पढ़ ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: किताब is feminine singular, so the vector is ली.

game.question_en: You want to say you've read the book — finished it, to yourself.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. पढ़ ली finishes it and keeps it with you; पढ़ दी would mean you read it aloud to somebody.

items.pronunciation_notes: Two short even beats: le le-naa. The stem and the vector sound almost identical, and that is correct.
items.gloss_en: to take and keep — लेना on both sides

learn.title_en: When the main verb and the vector are the same word
learn.explanation_en: ले लेना looks strange and is completely ordinary. लेना can serve as its own vector: ले is the stem, लिया the vector. मैंने पैसे ले लिए — I took the money and kept it. The doubling is not emphasis; it is the same completion-plus-inward meaning लेना always contributes, applied to a verb that already means "take". पैसे is masculine plural, so the vector is लिए. देना does exactly the same thing in the next level.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both correct. The vector adds that the taking is complete and the money stayed with you.

examples.note: पैसे is masculine plural, so लिए.
Imperative, and softer than plain लो.
चाबी is feminine, so ली.

common_error.why_en: पैसे is masculine plural, so the vector goes plural too.

practice.prompt_en: The object is पैसे. Complete the compound.
practice.question: मैंने पैसे ले ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: पैसे is masculine plural, so the vector is लिए.

game.question_en: You took the money, and you kept it.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct sentences. ले लिए adds that it is done and the money stayed with you; दे दिए would mean you handed it over instead.

learn.title_en: बना लिया — cooked, and it was mine
learn.explanation_en: बनाना is to make, and लेना puts the result on your own side of the ledger. मैंने खाना बना लिया means I cooked, and the food is for me. Hold on to this sentence, because the next level changes exactly one syllable and moves the food to somebody else. That pair — बना लिया against बना दिया — is the clearest demonstration of the whole लेना and देना distinction, which is why the two halves are taught back to back.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both correct. The plain form says you cooked; the vector says it is done and it was for you.

examples.note: For myself. खाना is masculine, so लिया.
चाय is feminine, so ली.
The inward sense is unmistakable here — the house is his.

common_error.why_en: The main verb is a bare stem: बना, not बनाया.

practice.prompt_en: The object is चाय. Complete the compound.
practice.question: मैंने चाय बना ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: चाय is feminine singular, so the vector is ली.

game.question_en: You cooked, and the food is for you.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. बना लिया keeps the food with you; बना दिया sends it to somebody else; the first simply says you cooked.

summary.recap_en: The object's gender and number land on the vector and nowhere else — पढ़ ली, ले लिए, बना ली. लेना can be its own vector, and ले लिया is completely ordinary Hindi.
summary.next_up_en: Next: देना, and the one syllable that moves the food across the table.

items.gloss_en: to tell — out with it, and done

learn.explanation_en: देना says the action is complete and its result goes away from the subject — to somebody else, or simply out of your hands. मैंने बता दिया is "I told them", and that is that. Compare मैंने बताया, which reports the telling without the finality. बताना already takes को on the person told, from Module 8, and the vector does not disturb that: मैंने उसे सब बता दिया. देना is transitive like लेना, so compounds on it take ने and the vector agrees with the object.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both correct. दिया adds that the telling is out of your hands now; the plain form just reports it.

examples.note: No object, so the neutral दिया.
The person told takes को, fused to उसे.

examples.hindi: उसने बता दिया कि वह नहीं आएगा।
examples.read_as: usne bataa diyaa ki vah nahiiṁ aaegaa.
examples.note: Decisive and settled — which is what दिया is doing here.

common_error.why_en: देना is transitive, so the compound requires ने.

practice.prompt_en: You told him, and the matter is out of your hands. Pick the vector.
practice.question: मैंने उसे सब बता ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: The telling goes outward, so देना.

game.question_en: You told them, and the matter is now settled.
game.explanation_en: All four are grammatical. बता दिया carries the finality; the plain form reports the telling; बता लिया would be odd here because telling naturally goes outward.

tts_strings: उसने बता दिया कि वह नहीं आएगा।

learn.title_en: One syllable moves the food across the table
learn.explanation_en: मैंने खाना बना लिया and मैंने खाना बना दिया differ by one syllable, and the difference is who the food is for. लिया keeps it with you; दिया sends it out. This is the clearest pair in the module and worth over-learning, because it is the entire लेना and देना distinction inside a single sentence. Everything else in these four levels is this fact applied to other verbs.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both correct. The plain form says you cooked and leaves out who it was for; दिया says it went to somebody else.

examples.note: For someone else.
For myself. Same verb, other direction.

examples.hindi: उसने मेरे लिए चाय बना दी।
examples.read_as: usne mere lie chaay banaa dii.
examples.note: चाय is feminine, so दी — and के लिए makes the direction explicit.

common_error.wrong: मैंने अपने लिए खाना बना दिया।
common_error.right: मैंने अपने लिए खाना बना लिया।
common_error.why_en: दिया sends the result outward, which clashes with "for myself". The sentence is well formed but its two halves disagree.

practice.prompt_en: You cooked for somebody else. Pick the vector.
practice.question: मैंने तुम्हारे लिए खाना बना ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: The food goes outward, so देना.

game.question_en: You cooked, and the food is for someone else.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. बना दिया sends the food outward. बना लिया would keep it with you, and the plain form leaves the question open.

tts_strings: उसने मेरे लिए चाय बना दी।

items.pronunciation_notes: Two short beats, de de-naa, exactly parallel to ले लेना.
items.gloss_en: to hand over — देना on both sides

learn.explanation_en: Like ले लेना, देना can be its own vector: दे is the stem, दिया the vector. मैंने पैसे दे दिए — I handed the money over. The doubling is not emphasis; it is completion plus outward direction, which is what देना always contributes, applied to a verb that already means "give". पैसे is masculine plural, so the vector is दिए. Put ले लिए and दे दिए side by side and you have the two directions at their clearest.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both correct. The vector adds that the handing over is complete and the money has gone.

examples.note: पैसे is masculine plural, so दिए.
किताब is feminine, so दी.
Imperative; दो is the तुम form of देना.

common_error.why_en: पैसे is masculine plural, so the vector is plural.

practice.prompt_en: The object is पैसे. Complete the compound.
practice.question: मैंने पैसे दे ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: पैसे is masculine plural, so the vector is दिए.

game.question_en: You handed the money over, and it is gone.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct sentences. दे दिए adds the finality; ले लिए is the opposite direction; the first simply reports the giving.

summary.recap_en: देना completes the action and sends its result outward — to somebody else, or out of your hands. बता दिया, बना दिया, दे दिया. Like लेना it is transitive, so the compound takes ने. And बना लिया against बना दिया is the pair to keep.
summary.next_up_en: Next: देना's second sense — decisiveness — and choosing between the two directions.

levels.title_en: Decisive देना, and choosing a direction
levels.title_hi: लिख दी · खोल दिया · ली या दी

learn.explanation_en: उसने चिट्ठी लिख दी. चिट्ठी is feminine, so the vector goes to दी and लिख does not move. The nuance is that the letter was written for somebody, or written and sent — out of the writer's hands either way. Set it beside उसने चिट्ठी लिख ली, which would mean she wrote it and kept it, and the difference is the same one you met with the food. The recipient, when named, takes को exactly as it always has.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both correct, and both feminine. The vector adds that the letter went to somebody.

examples.note: चिट्ठी is feminine, so दी. Written for somebody.
पता is masculine, so दिया.
The recipient takes को, fused to उसे.

common_error.why_en: चिट्ठी is feminine and the vector agrees with it.

practice.prompt_en: The object is चिट्ठी. Complete the compound.
practice.question: उसने चिट्ठी लिख ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: चिट्ठी is feminine singular, so the vector is दी.

game.question_en: You wrote the address down for them.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. लिख दिया sends it to them; लिख लिया would mean you noted it down for yourself, which is a perfectly good sentence about a different situation.

items.pronunciation_notes: ख is aspirated: khol, one syllable.

learn.title_en: देना for actions that cannot be taken back
learn.explanation_en: देना has a second sense that is not about giving at all: decisiveness. उसने दरवाज़ा खोल दिया — he opened the door, and it is open. Nothing is being handed to anybody; what देना adds is that the action is complete and not going to be undone. This is the sense behind a great many everyday compounds — कर दिया, छोड़ दिया, बंद कर दिया. The two senses are related if you look at them the right way: in both, the result has left the subject's control.

vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Both correct. The plain form reports the opening; दिया says it was done and the door stayed open.

examples.note: दरवाज़ा is masculine, so दिया. Done, and it stayed open.
खिड़की is feminine, so दी.
Decisive — and often, for somebody else. Both senses at once.

common_error.why_en: Bare stem before the vector: खोल, not खोला.

practice.prompt_en: The object is खिड़की. Complete the compound.
practice.question: मैंने खिड़की खोल ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: खिड़की is feminine singular, so the vector is दी.

game.question_en: The door was opened, decisively, and it stayed open.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct Hindi. खोल दिया carries the decisiveness; the plain form simply reports the opening.

items.gloss_en: inward or outward — choosing between them

learn.title_en: The same book, two directions, and a third option
learn.explanation_en: मैंने किताब पढ़ ली and मैंने किताब पढ़ दी are both correct and mean different things. ली keeps the reading with you: you read it, you finished it. दी sends it out: you read it aloud, to somebody. That is the whole distinction and it holds across every verb — लेना is inward, देना is outward. And the third option has been there the entire time: मैंने किताब पढ़ी, which says you read the book and nothing more. Choosing that one is a choice, not a failure to choose.

vectorless_equivalent.with_vector: मैंने किताब पढ़ ली। / मैंने किताब पढ़ दी।
vectorless_equivalent.difference_en: Three correct sentences. Inward, outward, and neutral — and the neutral one is the right answer whenever you have nothing to add.

examples.note: To myself, and finished.
To somebody else.
Neutral, and still the right choice when you mean nothing more.

common_error.why_en: The reading was for him, so the vector has to turn outward. ली would contradict the उसे.

practice.prompt_en: You read the book aloud to him. Pick the vector.
practice.question: मैंने उसे किताब पढ़ ___ ।
practice.explanation_en: The reading goes outward to him, so देना — and किताब is feminine, so दी.

game.question_en: You read the book to yourself and finished it.
game.explanation_en: All four are correct. पढ़ ली is the inward, finished one. पढ़ दी would send it outward, and the first is the neutral report.

summary.recap_en: देना's second sense is decisiveness rather than giving — खोल दिया, कर दिया. And the choice between ली and दी is a choice of direction: inward or outward. The plain form is always the third option, and picking it is a decision rather than an omission.
summary.next_up_en: Next: जाना — and the compound that refuses ने even though its main verb is transitive.
